key_insight: DFT simulations predict that certain shear strains transform monolayer h-BN into an ordered orthorhombic pmmm phase with a narrow band gap of approximately 0.65 eV.
engineering_relevance: Strain-induced phase transformation could enable band-gap engineering in 2D boron nitride, shifting it from a wide-gap insulator toward a semiconductor.
method: First-principles DFT with pseudopotentials and PBE exchange-correlation.
Direction- and strain-type-dependent structural transformation analysis.
Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics to assess thermal stability.
evidence_signal: Simulations demonstrate thermal stability of the predicted orthorhombic phase up to approximately 900 K and indicate a band gap near 0.65 eV.
watch_item: The phase is computationally predicted; experimental accessibility under strong shear and the accuracy of the PBE band gap require validation.
paper_title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
